derivation: STANDARDS-DERIVED. Citation statuses observe source_status_ceiling. EN 17007 SPP is the spine. IEC 61968-6 cl. 4.2 has no procurement component; goods sit on MM and invoices on FIN. ASCM SCOR v14 is named in the pack as structural precedent only and is not used as content. PIDX is excluded.
taxonomy_origin: TAXONOMY ORIGIN, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT FACT FROM THE DERIVATION ABOVE. The derivation line describes where FIELD CONTENT comes from: every field value traces to a standard, a regulation or a recognised industry body and carries its citation. It does NOT describe where the taxonomy comes from. Which processes exist, how they are grouped and what they are called is a practitioner synthesis of delivered implementations, generalised until it is product- and client-neutral. Of the 102 process groups, 43 originate in programme material, 28 in domain research, 20 in a published source and 11 in folder and file names; the provenance layer grades every one and names what to read next. This model is DELIVERED PRACTICE SPECIFIED AGAINST STANDARDS, not a standard turned into a model - and saying so is not a weakness. A taxonomy proven in delivery and then held against the standards is a stronger claim than one derived from a standard and never built.
field_set: EN 17007:2017 cl. 5.2 maintenance process profile, corroborated by ISO 9001:2015 cl. 4.4.1 a) to h).
gaps: IEC 61968-6:2015 cl. 4.2 has no procurement, document or health-and-safety component. Requisitions, orders and catalogues sit on MM; invoices on FIN. The absence is recorded rather than inventing a code.

ASCM SCOR v14 is listed in the pack as structural precedent only, not a content source. It is not cited for process. APQC 4.0 Deliver Physical Products (pcf_id 10215) is cross-industry manufacturing; only APQC 10 and 14 carry utility content. 14.4.1 Procure meter components (19326) is the assignment-pack touch and is partial.
PIDX is excluded by the pack. There is no standardised supplier catalogue, ASN, PO-ACK or invoice payload for this domain. 13.7 exchange processes are judgment on channel.

Vehicle stock (13.3) is not a standards domain. CIM has Vehicle and MaterialItem; IEC 61968-6 has MM, not a fleet component. Truck lists, truck-to-truck transfer, in-transit type and fleet search are judgment.

No pack standard specifies intermittent-demand forecasting, safety-stock arithmetic, multi-echelon positioning, insurance-spare definition, item-master content, commodity-code scheme, consignment/VMI, or a supplier scorecard. SPP.1/SPP.2/DTA.5 are the closest names.
18 CFR 101 continuing plant inventory is the PROPERTY record (5.3 / 12.1), not storeroom stock. Cycle-count adjustments are not unitisation.

NERC CIP-013 is bulk-power cyber supply chain, pack-scoped to 16.0. 16 U.S.C. 824o keeps it off distribution materials. 13.7.1 qualifies goods suppliers, not field contractors (16.1) and not CIP vendors.

EN 17007 SPP is spare parts for maintenance. Construction material, compatible units and customer-contribution jobs still flow through 13 because that is where MM lives; SPP titles are a stretch for construction line items and are labelled by using ACT.2 at 13.1.1.

2.4.4 defines that the job needs material; 13.1.1 explodes it to stock items. 13.2.2 issues at the window; 13.3.3 charges van consumption. 13.4.3 matches the PO; 13.2.1 puts away. 13.4.4 matches the invoice. Those splits are deliberate.
EN 13306 Annex E criticality is paywalled and cited by title only at 13.5.7. EN 13269 is contracting and is scoped by the pack to 16.0.

merge_corrections.what: citation form: a status may not claim more than the citation string supports. 'clause-verified' without a clause dropped to 'consensus'; an asserted absence dropped to 'judgment'.

notation.why on six SPEC processes said 'standing' where the work is a determination. The class is right and unchanged; the reason was not. Five of them produce a value - a forecast, a stock level, an allocation, a criticality class, a supplier score - and pass the DMN test on shape. They are SPEC because no source states the rule, and inventing one would breach the derivation rule. SCHEMA.md now carries that as the second SPEC case.

ISO 55001:2024 cl. 8.3 was cited with ISO 9001's wording. The clause number is right; its title is Outsourcing. 'Control of externally provided processes, products and services' is ISO 9001:2015 cl. 8.4. A status of clause-verified asserts the clause number AND its title, so a borrowed title is an unearned status.
